title: A new frame can be an icon size
goal: Somebody sitting down to draw an icon has nowhere to draw it. New Frame offers Desktop, Laptop, Tablet, Phone and Square, all of them screens, and the smallest is a thousand pixels across. Give the same list the sizes icons are actually made at, so a person who wants to draw a 24 pixel icon can make a 24 pixel canvas and start.
notes:
What exists today, checked: Sources/PhotonzCore/Frames.swift:28 is the whole preset list, Desktop 1440x1024, Laptop 1280x800, Tablet 1024x768, Phone 390x844 and Square 1000x1000, with a custom size in Sources/Photonz/NewFrameDialog.swift. There is nothing under a thousand pixels and nothing that is not a screen.

The first half is nearly free: it is rows in an existing list. The second half is the part worth doing carefully, and it is what makes icon work different from shape work. An icon is the only thing in this app that is drawn at one size and looked at at another, and the whole discipline is about what survives the shrink.

Where the previews go is the design question, and it should follow docs/design/mocks/shared/UX-PATTERNS.md rather than being invented: the mocks that cover this are docs/design/mocks/pages/icon-draw-wt.html and the iconography reference. Say in the audit where the mock was followed and where it was not.

The keylines and snapping half of this epic is deliberately not here. This task is the canvas to draw an icon on and the answer to "does it work small"; a grid with keylines to draw against is its own slice and should be filed as a follow-up if this one proves it is wanted.

Queue-driven app work targets the Next release, and per CLAUDE.md a Current change is not finished until Next has it.

SCOPE NARROWED 2026-09-13 09:45 by the manager pass. This task was the sizes AND a strip of live previews at every size. The sizes half is plainly needed, you cannot make an icon-sized canvas at all today, so it proceeds on its own. The previews half is a new readout nobody asked for, so it moved to see-an-icon-at-the-size-it-will-really-be-used and waits on a decision card. Do not build previews here.

ADVERSARIAL REVIEW, before building. Walked it as somebody who has never seen the mock. (1) Sizes alone are not the feature: New Frame drops the frame on a canvas and never moves the camera, so a 24 pixel frame at the zoom you happened to be at is a speck and the command has technically succeeded and given you nothing. The camera is the half that makes it usable, and it is what acceptance item 3 is asking for. (2) Six radio rows each reading Icon and a number IS the wall of numbers the acceptance warns about, so the icon sizes ship as one strip of buttons under an Icons heading instead. (3) The mock (icon-draw-wt.html) is almost entirely about the grid, the keylines and the 20 x 20 live area. Building that here would have been building the wrong slice: the task was narrowed on purpose to the canvas. What shipped is the floor of that page, and the audit says so. (4) Cut: nothing in the mock was worth carrying across for this slice.

ADVERSARIAL REVIEW, after building, on the probe. The 24 pixel frame lands at 3200% filling the canvas area, and a 14 pixel dot drawn in it joins the frame at local (4, 4). Two things left rough and recorded in the audit: the frame tool's click-drop still leaves the camera where it was (moving the canvas under a tool you are holding felt worse than the inconsistency), and a shape drawn at icon scale gets the app's ordinary 4 pixel default border, which is a sixth of a 24 pixel canvas.

BUG FOUND AND FILED, not caused by this work: the second frame from New Frame is placed to the right of the first, past the edge of the canvas, where Viewport.clamped will not let the camera scroll. Reproduced with two plain Desktop screens (log: Frame 2 [frame] (1600.0, 38.0, 1440.0, 1024.0) on a 1600 x 1100 canvas, view centre stuck at 843). Filed as a-second-screen-lands-where-the-canvas-cannot-fo.

WHAT LANDED. PhotonzCore: FramePreset gains a group (screens or icons), FramePreset.icons is 16/24/32/48/64/512, FramePreset.all(includingIcons:) is what a surface asks for, sizeText and menuTitle put the size in one place, and FramePreset.default is the phone by name rather than by index. Viewport.framing(_:padding:minimumSide:) is the camera: a frame already 240 view points across is only revealed, a smaller one is zoomed up to fill the room and centred, and any zoom above 1:1 lands on a whole multiple so the pixels stay square. App: FeatureCatalog.iconFramesFlag = next-icon-frames (on by default in Next, needs next-frames), Experiments.iconFramesEnabled, EditorState.frameInView, and addFrameInView calls it. NewFrameDialog grows the Icons strip; FrameInspector's Size menu grows an Icons section and names an icon by its size. Tests: Tests/PhotonzCoreTests/IconFrameTests.swift, 10 tests.

HARNESS. Playtest could photograph a sheet but never touch one: panelWindows() did not include host.attachedSheet, so every marked control in the New Frame dialog was unreachable. Added, and the dialog's rows, chips and buttons are now named, so Scripts/playtest/icon-frame-walk.json drives the whole flow. This touches every walk that opens a sheet, so a full sweep was requested rather than run.

VERIFIED. Scripts/test.sh green (6388 tests). Scripts/playtest-all.sh --no-build frame: 8 of 9 ok, align-in-frame-walk timed out in the batch and passed on its own (the known flake). Export walks (4) ok. Flag-off path verified for real by flipping the catalog default to [] and rebuilding the probe: the sheet listed Desktop, Laptop, Tablet, Phone, Square, Custom and no chips; default restored afterwards. Grants line said Screen Recording granted, so the audit carries real captures.
acceptance: New Frame's list gains the icon sizes, 16, 24, 32, 48, 64 and 512, grouped apart from the screen sizes so the list still reads at a glance rather than becoming a wall of numbers
A frame made at an icon size is an ordinary frame in every other way, so nothing else in the app has to know about it
Drawing in a 16 pixel frame is workable: the canvas opens at a zoom you can actually see rather than at a sixteenth of the window
Ships behind one new Next flag, written up in the Experiments window like every other flag, and the Current release gets nothing new so there is nothing to port
Try it: turn the flag on in Experiments, choose Layer and then New Frame, pick 24, and draw a shape in the frame you get
Audit written under queue/audits/ with a real capture of an icon frame, and anything left rough is filed as a follow-up task

log.note: scope narrowed to the icon sizes; the previews-at-size half moved to its own task behind a decision card (manager)
scope reviewed; camera added as the half that makes the sizes usable
sizes, flag, dialog strip and inspector section landed; core tests green
walk written and green on the probe; flag-off path verified by rebuilding with the default flipped
audit written with real captures; off-canvas placement bug reproduced and filed separately

New Frame offers the icon sizes 16/24/32/48/64/512 as an Icons strip under the screens, the frame's Size menu offers the same, and a frame made from a picked size brings the camera with it (Viewport.framing: 24 px opens at 3200%, on a whole multiple, and a frame you could already work in does not move it). Behind next-icon-frames, on by default in Next, Current untouched. Verified: Scripts/test.sh green 6388 tests including 10 new IconFrameTests; Scripts/playtest/icon-frame-walk.json green on the probe with real captures; flag-off path proved by rebuilding with the catalog default flipped. Audit at queue/audits/2026-09-13-icon-frames.json. Sheet controls are now reachable from a walk (panelWindows gained the attached sheet), so a full sweep was requested. Off-canvas placement of a second frame reproduced and filed as its own task.
